newsitem.title: USA: Rexrodt - Bonn must stick to goal of halving jobless.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt - Bonn must stick to goal of halving jobless.

text.p: Germany's government must stick by its stated goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000, German economics minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Saturday.

In response to a question suggesting that the goal was unrealistic, Rexrodt said at a breakfast briefing: "This is a goal which has been set jointly by the government, the trade unions and industry...It is a goal, and an ambitious goal.
"And we are continuing to strive for it. It would be a poor show if we were to abandon it," he added.
The aim of halving Germany's 4-1/2 million unemployed in the next three years has been labelled unrealistic by independent economists.
Germany's IFO research institute said last week that the jobless queues could only be cut at such a rate if the German ecnomy grew by 5.75 percent per year over the next three years.
Bonn is predicting economic growth of no more than 2.5 percent this year.
Rexrodt is taking part in the summit meeting of the Group of Seven industrialized nations in Denver, Colarado. Unemployment is expected to rank high on the agenda for the meeting.
